title: Knapsack interdiction
description: A bilevel knapsack: the leader locks items within a budget, then the follower packs the rest within a capacity; the solutions are the leader's choices that keep the follower's best profit at or below a bound (Sigma-2-complete; Caprara, Carvalho, Lodi and Woeginger). The check packs a knapsack that beats the bound, preferring few items ('optimal'), and the refinement locks one of them. With bound = 24 there is no solution: 25 is the best the leader can do.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The items. Added to every solver.
fragments.text: % The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): locked items within the budget.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a set of locked items whose costs stay within the leader's budget.
{ lock(I) : item(I,_,_,_) }.
:- #sum { C,I : lock(I), item(I,C,_,_) } > budget.
#show lock/1.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the locked items.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for a packing of the remaining items that beats the bound (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: the follower packs items that are not locked, within the capacity,
% with a profit above the bound.
{ pack(I) : item(I,_,_,_) }.
:- pack(I), lock(I).
:- #sum { W,I : pack(I), item(I,_,W,_) } > capacity.
:- #sum { P,I : pack(I), item(I,_,_,P) } <= bound.
#show pack/1.

% The packing stays possible as long as none of its items is locked.
relevant(lock(I)) :- pack(I).
% A packing with few items gives a short clause.
#minimize { 1,I : pack(I) }.

fragments.name: check_best
fragments.text:
% The follower's best response: a packing of unlocked items within the capacity with the
% largest profit, if that profit is above the bound (variant best-response).
{ pack(I) : item(I,_,_,_) }.
:- pack(I), lock(I).
:- #sum { W,I : pack(I), item(I,_,W,_) } > capacity.
:- #sum { P,I : pack(I), item(I,_,_,P) } <= bound.
#show pack/1.

relevant(lock(I)) :- pack(I).
#maximize { P,I : pack(I), item(I,_,_,P) }.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# 'optimal' returns a counterexample that is optimal for the #minimize statement of
# the check: a packing with as few items as possible, hence a clause with few literals.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M), optimal)
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

instances.facts:
% item(I,Cost,Weight,Profit): the leader can lock item I at the given cost; the
% follower can pack it (if it is not locked) with the given weight and profit.
item(1,3,4,9).  item(2,2,3,7).  item(3,4,5,12). item(4,1,2,4).
item(5,3,6,13). item(6,2,4,8).  item(7,5,7,16). item(8,1,3,5).

item(1,3,4,9).  item(2,2,3,7).  item(3,4,5,12). item(4,1,2,4).
item(5,3,6,13). item(6,2,4,8).  item(7,5,7,16). item(8,1,3,5).

item(4,2,5,9). item(5,1,1,2). item(6,2,3,5).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Any packing above the bound, not the one with the fewest items.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Up to three packings per candidate, one clause each.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        for X in C.models(assume G(M), limit 3):
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M), optimal)
    if X:
        A.add(G.clause(M, X))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

generators.name: items
generators.description: n random items: cost 1..4, weight 2..7, profit about twice the weight. Set budget, capacity and bound as constants.
generators.text:
% items: n items with a random cost (1..4), weight (2..7) and profit (twice the weight plus 0..3)
item(I,C,W,2*W+E) :- I = 1..n, C = @int(1, 4, cost, I), W = @int(2, 7, weight, I), E = @int(0, 3, extra, I).
#show item/4.

spaces.name: items
spaces.description: Size items with small costs, weights and profits.
spaces.text:
% every item list: items 1..size with cost 1..2, weight 1..3 and profit 1..3
iid(1..size).
1 { item(I,C,W,P) : C = 1..2, W = 1..3, P = 1..3 } 1 :- iid(I).
